examples.title: Shopping cart total
examples.description: A list of dictionaries, a generator expression for the subtotal, Decimal for exact money arithmetic and a receipt formatted with alignment.
examples.code:
from decimal import Decimal

cart = [
    {"item": "Notebook", "price": Decimal("4.50"), "qty": 3},
    {"item": "Pen", "price": Decimal("1.25"), "qty": 10},
    {"item": "Backpack", "price": Decimal("39.99"), "qty": 1},
]

for line in cart:
    line_total = line["price"] * line["qty"]
    print(f"{line['item']:<10}{line['qty']:>3} x {line['price']:>6} = {line_total:>7}")

subtotal = sum(line["price"] * line["qty"] for line in cart)
tax = (subtotal * Decimal("0.20")).quantize(Decimal("0.01"))
print(f"{'Subtotal':<24}{subtotal:>7}")
print(f"{'Tax 20%':<24}{tax:>7}")
print(f"{'Total':<24}{subtotal + tax:>7}")
examples.output:
Notebook    3 x   4.50 =   13.50
Pen        10 x   1.25 =   12.50
Backpack    1 x  39.99 =   39.99
Subtotal                  65.99
Tax 20%                   13.20
Total                     79.19

examples.title: CSV sales report
examples.description: Writes a small CSV file with csv.DictWriter, reads it back with csv.DictReader, converts the numeric columns and prints revenue per region.
examples.code:
import csv

sales = [
    {"region": "North", "product": "Lamp", "units": 4, "price": 25.0},
    {"region": "South", "product": "Chair", "units": 2, "price": 80.0},
    {"region": "North", "product": "Desk", "units": 1, "price": 150.0},
]

with open("sales.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=["region", "product", "units", "price"])
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(sales)

revenue = {}
with open("sales.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    for row in csv.DictReader(file):
        amount = int(row["units"]) * float(row["price"])
        revenue[row["region"]] = revenue.get(row["region"], 0) + amount

for region, amount in sorted(revenue.items()):
    print(f"{region:<8}{amount:>8.2f}")

examples.title: Fetch JSON from a web API
examples.description: Calls the free JSONPlaceholder test API with urllib, parses the JSON response and prints a summary. Needs an internet connection; the sample data never changes.
examples.code:
import json
from urllib.request import urlopen

URL = "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users"

with urlopen(URL, timeout=10) as response:
    users = json.load(response)

print(len(users), "users")
for user in users[:3]:
    print(f"{user['name']:<18}{user['email']:<26}{user['address']['city']}")
examples.output:
10 users
Leanne Graham     Sincere@april.biz         Gwenborough
Ervin Howell      Shanna@melissa.tv         Wisokyburgh
Clementine Bauch  Nathan@yesenia.net        McKenziehaven

examples.title: Count lines in every text file
examples.description: Creates a few sample files with pathlib, then walks the folder with glob() and prints the number of non-empty lines in each file plus the total.
examples.code:
from pathlib import Path

folder = Path("notes")
folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
(folder / "monday.txt").write_text("Plan\nWrite\n\nReview\n", encoding="utf-8")
(folder / "tuesday.txt").write_text("Test\nShip\n", encoding="utf-8")

total = 0
for path in sorted(folder.glob("*.txt")):
    lines = [line for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]
    print(f"{path.name:<14}{len(lines):>3}")
    total += len(lines)
print(f"{'total':<14}{total:>3}")
